summary: The study investigates the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of SrTiO3 thin films using Sr(thd)2 and Ti(Oi-C3H7)4 precursors with remote plasma activated or thermal H2O vapor as oxidant. The films were grown at temperatures ranging from 190 to 270°C. The as-grown films were amorphous and showed a low effective dielectric constant. The study also discusses the impact of postdeposition annealing (PDA) on the crystallization and electrical properties of the films, highlighting the importance of a crystallized seed layer in improving microstructure and leakage current performance. The best electrical properties achieved were an equivalent oxide thickness of 0.45 nm and a leakage current density of 1×10−3 A/cm2 at 1 V.
